name: Jeep Wrangler
evaluation_notes:
JK (2012–2018) or JL (2018+) generation. Avoid 2007–2011 JK with the 3.8L engine — 2012+ Pentastar 3.6L only. Buyer wants a capable, reliable off-road vehicle, not a project or daily driver. Clean title essential. JK sweet spot: 2014–2018, 60k–110k miles, $13k–$20k. JL sweet spot: 2018–2021, 50k–100k miles, $18k–$25k. Reward: Rubicon trim (locking diffs, sway bar disconnect), documented service history.

AFTERMARKET VALUE — quality builds command a real premium; factor installed cost into estimated_market_value. Reward these named-brand upgrades: Warn winch (9.5i, Zeon, VR10) adds $800–$1,500; ARB, Warn, or Smittybilt steel bumpers add $600–$2,000; Old Man Emu, Bilstein, Fox, or Rubicon Express 2–3" lift with quality install adds $1,500–$3,000; BFG KO2 or Falken Wildpeak AT3W tires (if recent) add $800–$1,200; ARB or Prinsu roof rack adds $500–$1,500; MaxTrax, hi-lift jack, recovery kit adds $300–$700. A well-documented build with receipts is worth $3k–$8k over a stock example.

Penalize: unknown brand lift, extreme lift (4"+) without professional documentation, evidence of off-road abuse without maintenance, modifications that removed factory safety equipment. Flag: death wobble mentions, rust on tub floor or rockers, soft top damage, airbag removal.

name: Jeep Gladiator
evaluation_notes:
2020+ only (JT generation, the only generation made). Shares the JL Wrangler platform and Pentastar 3.6L drivetrain with a mid-size truck bed. Buyer wants capability and utility, not a daily driver. Rubicon trim strongly preferred (locking front and rear diffs, disconnecting sway bar). Sport S and Overland acceptable at the right price. Sweet spot: 2020–2022, under 70k miles, $22k–$30k.

AFTERMARKET VALUE — same quality brands apply as Wrangler. Warn winch adds $800–$1,500; ARB/Warn steel bumpers add $600–$2,000; Fox or Bilstein 2–3" lift adds $1,500–$3,000; BFG KO2 or Falken Wildpeak tires add $800–$1,200; bed rack or Gobi/Prinsu roof rack adds $500–$1,500; bed slide, drawer system (Decked, Drawer System), or slide-out kitchen adds $500–$2,000. A well-built Gladiator with quality mods and receipts is worth $4k–$10k over stock.

Reward: factory tow package, hard top. Penalize: Mojave trim (desert suspension, not optimal for rock crawling), near-MSRP pricing, unknown lift brands, modifications without documentation. Flag: frame rust, accident history, death wobble.

name: Toyota 4Runner
evaluation_notes:
5th gen only (2014+). Most reliable SUV on the market — 1GR-FE V6 runs indefinitely with basic maintenance, timing chain not belt. TRD Off Road or TRD Pro preferred (KDSS suspension, locking rear diff). SR5 4WD is acceptable. Sweet spot: 2015–2020, 70k–130k miles, $18k–$30k.

AFTERMARKET VALUE — 4Runner builds are common and well-documented. Old Man Emu BP-51 or Icon Vehicle Dynamics 2–3" lift adds $2,000–$4,000; ARB front bumper with integrated winch mount adds $800–$2,000; Warn or ARB winch adds $800–$1,500; Front Runner or ARB roof rack with awning adds $1,000–$2,500; BFG KO2 or Falken Wildpeak tires add $800–$1,200; ARB or TRD skid plates add $300–$800; drawer/sleeping platform adds $500–$2,000. A well-built 4Runner with receipts and quality parts is worth $3k–$8k over stock.

Penalize: 2WD models, near-MSRP on recent years, unknown lift brands. Flag: rust (check frame on high-mileage examples), no service history, accident damage.

name: Lexus GX460
evaluation_notes:
2014+ only (post-interior refresh). Same platform and 4.6L V8 as the 4Runner but with a luxury interior and KDSS standard on all trims. Outstanding off-road capability with a comfortable cabin. Sweet spot: 2015–2019, 60k–110k miles, $18k–$30k.

AFTERMARKET VALUE — GX460 builds tend to be tasteful and well-funded. Old Man Emu or Icon lift 2" adds $1,500–$3,000; ARB front bumper adds $800–$2,000; Warn or ARB winch adds $800–$1,500; Front Runner or Yakima roof rack with awning adds $800–$2,000; BFG KO2 or Falken Wildpeak tires add $800–$1,200; interior upgrades (Lexus or aftermarket) add value too if documented. A GX460 with a quality documented build is worth $2k–$6k over stock — buyers of this platform tend to spend well.

Reward: full service history, low miles for year, Premium trim or above. Penalize: accident history, deferred maintenance, near-MSRP on recent years, modifications that compromise the luxury interior. Flag: check for oil consumption on high-mileage examples, suspension air bag leaks.

name: Toyota FJ Cruiser
evaluation_notes:
All years 2007–2014 (discontinued). Same proven 4.0L 1GR-FE V6 and 4WD system as the 4Runner — extremely reliable, cult following keeps values stable. TRD package preferred (locking rear diff, skid plates). Poor rear visibility is a known design quirk, not a defect. Sweet spot: 2010–2014, 80k–140k miles, $13k–$20k.

AFTERMARKET VALUE — FJ Cruisers are heavily modded vehicles with a passionate community; well-built examples command strong premiums. Old Man Emu BP-51 or Icon lift adds $2,000–$3,500; ARB front and rear bumpers add $1,000–$3,000; Warn winch adds $800–$1,500; roof rack (FJ-specific Prinsu, Wilco, or ARB) adds $800–$2,000; BFG KO2 or Falken Wildpeak tires add $800–$1,200; skid plates add $300–$800; snorkel adds $300–$700. A well-documented build on a clean FJ Cruiser with receipts is worth $4k–$10k over a stock example and should be scored accordingly.

Reward: TRD package with factory locking rear diff, documented service history, rust-free southern or western state vehicle. Penalize: rust on frame or wheel wells — these rust badly in northern/salt-belt climates, check undercarriage photos carefully. Flag: frame rust (deal breaker), transmission slipping, no service records. Hold to a high value standard — only surface as a deal if price is genuinely below market.
